title: Detecting the emulsion side on plates

posts.topic_title: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.author: Tom B.
posts.post_subject: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.content_md: You can either breathe on them (no condensation occurs on the emulsion side because the gelatin absorbs the moisture), or just look at the edge of the glass with a safelight - the cleanest (non-ragged) edge is the emulsion side. With a bit of practice you can detect the difference in the dark by rubbing your thumbnail along the edge..

posts.topic_title: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.content_md: You can also put the plate between your lips and pull. The side that sticks is the emulsion.

posts.topic_title: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.author: edelbrp
posts.post_subject: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.content_md:
If all the plates are oriented the same way, you can label the box 'emulsion this side ->'

If you don't know (or forgot), I use the two finger method: spit on your thumb and index finger and pinch them together a few times. Now do the same motion with the plate between them, and it should be easy to feel which side is the sticky emulsion side. (I'm a little wary of chemical coated glass plates on my lips. ;')

-Phil

posts.post_subject: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** You can also put the plate between your lips and pull. The side that sticks is the emulsion.

But would you want to do that with a dichromate-laden plate?

posts.topic_title: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.post_subject: Detecting the emulsion side on plates
posts.content_md:
> **MichaelH:** But would you want to do that with a dichromate-laden plate?

Definitely not! Yikes.

I look at the edges of my plates, where the glass was cut. If I focus very closely, I can see a slightly ragged edge where the gelatin does not exactly follow the underlying glass. (I cut my plates from a larger plate that has already been coated.)
